extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians and programmers needing reference for PARI functions)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions (matrix, quadratic-form, set and vector utilities) describing semantics, preconditions, flags, return formats, and examples. Useful for implementing, calling, or debugging PARI/GP code.

rubrics_metrics.name: matqr behavior and flag semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute QR decomposition; with flag=1 return orthogonal matrix as sequence of Householder transforms rather than explicit Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If [Q,R] = matqr(M) and [q,r] = matqr(M,1) then r = R and mathouseholder(q,M) is close to R; mathouseholder(q, matid(#M)) == Q~ (inverse of Q). Raises an error if precision is too low or x is singular. Library syntax: GEN matqr(GEN M, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: matrank (matrix rank)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the rank of matrix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long rank(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix (construction from expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an m × n matrix whose coefficients are given by an expression expr with parameters X (row index 1..m) and Y (column index 1..n); omitted last params fill zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: matrix(m,n,{X},{Y},{expr=0}). If one of the last 3 parameters omitted, fill with zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixqz (integral matrix with coprime minors / HNF bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given A ∈ Mm,n(Q), behavior depends on p: for p≥0 produce B ∈ Mm,n(Z) with ImQB = ImQA and GCD of all n×n minors coprime to p (p=0 => GCD=1). For p=-1 return HNF basis Zn ∩ ImZA. For p=-2 return HNF basis Zn ∩ ImQA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show computing minors and integral B with coprime minors. Syntax: GEN matrixqz0(GEN A, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsize (rows and columns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a row vector [#rows, #columns] for vector or matrix x (1 for row vector, 1 for column vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matsize(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsnf (Smith normal form / elementary divisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Output vector of elementary divisors (diagonal of Smith normal form) normalized so dn | dn-1 | ... | d1. Supports options through flag bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag bits: 1 => complete output [U,V,D] with unimodular U,V; 2 => allow polynomial entries (input must be square); 4 => cleanup: delete elementary divisors equal to 1 (shortened output) and allow input as preexisting [U,V,D] or vector of divisors. Syntax: GEN matsnf0(GEN X, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolve (solve linear system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve M X = B for invertible matrix M and column vector B. Uses Dixon p-adic lifting for integral input, Gaussian elimination otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent (but faster) to M^-1 * B. Library syntax mentions GEN gauss(GEN M, GEN B) and for integral input GEN ZM_gauss(GEN M, GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolvemod (solve modular congruence systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integral matrix M, vector D of non-negative integer moduli, and integral vector B, find a small integer solution to M x ≡ b (mod di) if exists; otherwise return 0. Shorthand: single integer for B or D applies same value to all entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 return all solutions as [x,u] where x is one small solution and columns of u are basis of homogeneous solutions. Examples and alternative functions: GEN gaussmodulo (flag=0) and GEN gaussmodulo2 (flag=1). Syntax: GEN matsolvemod0(GEN M, GEN D, GEN B, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsupplement (extend independent columns to basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a matrix whose columns are linearly independent, find a square invertible matrix whose first columns are the columns of x (supplement to a basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises an error if columns are not independent. Raises an error for 0-column matrix due to design limitation. Syntax: GEN suppl(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mattranspose (transpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose of x (also x~). Applies to vectors and matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtrans(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: minpoly (minimal polynomial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the minimal polynomial P (monic) of A with respect to variable v, i.e., monic polynomial P of minimal degree with P(A)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN minpoly(GEN A, long v = -1) where v is a variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: norml2 (square of L2-norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of the L2-norm: for scalars the square of complex modulus, recursively sum squares for polynomial/vector/matrix components to yield usual |xi|^2 and sum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: norml2([1,2,3])=14, norml2([1,2;3,4])=30. Syntax: GEN gnorml2(GEN x). Note: real t_QUADs not supported for scalar case.

rubrics_metrics.name: normlp (Lp-norm / sup norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lp-norm of x; if p omitted or +oo, return sup norm (max of component norms). Otherwise recursively compute (sum normlp(xi,p)^p)^(1/p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show vector and matrix uses. Syntax: GEN gnormlp(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfauto (automorphism group of quadratic form lattice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given square symmetric integer matrix G representing a positive definite quadratic form, output automorphism group of the associated lattice as [order, generators].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation can be lengthy for large dimension (requires minimal vectors). G can be qfisominit structure. Interface experimental and may change. Algorithm by Plesken & Souvignier. Syntax: GEN qfauto0(GEN G, GEN fl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfautoexport (export automorphism group to GAP/Magma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Export matrix group (output of qfauto) as string suitable for GAP (flag=0) or Magma (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates exporting and using GAP to compute order. Syntax: GEN qfautoexport(GEN qfa, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbil (obsolete alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete function; use qfeval instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax kept for backwards compatibility: GEN qfbil(GEN x, GEN y, GEN q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfeval (evaluate binary quadratic forms and polar form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate binary quadratic form q (symmetric matrix) at vector x; if y present evaluate polar form at (x,y); if q omitted use standard Euclidean scalar product (identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roughly x~ * q * y but faster and tolerant to row/column distinctions. Special cases: q omitted handled faster; accepts t_MAT inputs to return Gram matrix; accepts t_QFI/t_QFR and converts more efficiently; when x is t_MAT with integer coefficients and q is t_QFI/QFR, returns q ◦ M. Many speed comparisons/examples shown. Syntax: GEN qfeval0(GEN q = NULL, GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfgaussred (decomposition into squares)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose quadratic form q into sum of squares form represented by matrix whose diagonal entries are coefficients of squares and off-diagonals represent bilinear forms: q(x) = sum_i aii (xi + sum_{j!=i} aij xj)^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular matrices supported (some diagonal coefficients may vanish). qfgaussred_positive assumes positive definiteness and is faster; returns NULL if negative norm vector occurs. Syntax: GEN qfgaussred(GEN q).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfisom (isometry between quadratic forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given square symmetric integer positive definite matrices G and H, return invertible S with G = tS H S (isomorphism between lattices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation can be lengthy (requires minimal vectors). G can be qfisominit structure for efficiency. Algorithm follows Plesken & Souvignier. Syntax: GEN qfisom0(GEN G, GEN H, GEN fl = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfisominit (precompute invariants for isomorphism testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an isom structure for G (square symmetric integer positive definite) to speed up isomorphism computations with other forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interface experimental. Optional fl is a t_VEC with two components: fl[1] depth of scalar product combination; fl[2] max level of Bacher polynomials. Optional m parameter: set of vectors of norm up to max diagonal entry (matrix or from qfminim); otherwise minimal vectors computed (can be very lengthy). Syntax: GEN qfisominit0(GEN G, GEN fl = NULL, GEN m = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfjacobi (Jacobi eigenvalue algorithm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Jacobi's eigenvalue algorithm to real symmetric matrix A; returns [L,V] where L vector of real eigenvalues sorted increasing and V is orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show high precision and orthogonality checks. Syntax: GEN jacobi(GEN A, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflll (LLL reduction for lattice columns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply LLL algorithm to columns of matrix x; returns unimodular T so that x·T is LLL-reduced basis. Columns may be linearly dependent; if not maximal rank T not square. LLL parameters are (0.51,0.99).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags: 0 default (exact or floating input rescaled to integers), 1 assume integral and use approximate Gram-Schmidt with adaptive precision (Nguyen-Stehlé), 2 partially reduced basis (Peter Montgomery algorithm) faster but not LLL-reduced, 4 return [K,T] where K columns basis of integer kernel and T reduces image, 5 like 4 but polynomial coefficients allowed, 8 same as 0 but polynomial coefficients allowed. Alternative entry points: GEN lll(GEN x) (flag=0), GEN lllint(GEN x) (flag=1), GEN lllkerim(GEN x) (flag=4). Guidance: avoid partial reduction if eventual LLL desired (it slows eventual LLL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qflllgram (LLL from Gram matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as qflll but input G is Gram matrix G = x~ * x (square symmetric real matrix corresponding to quadratic form), not direct coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags similar to qflll: 0 assume exact/float and rescale, 1 integral with approximate Gram-Schmidt, 4 gives kernel and reduced image, 5 polynomial coefficients allowed. Syntax: GEN qflllgram0(GEN G, long flag). Other entry points: GEN lll-gram(GEN G), GEN lllgramint(GEN G), GEN lllgramkerim(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfminim (enumerate short vectors / minimal vectors)
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive definite quadratic form x, enumerate vectors with norm ≤ b using Fincke–Pohst algorithm, store at most m vectors (no limit if m omitted); if b omitted search minimal non-zero vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag behavior: flag=0 (default) returns at most 2m vectors and a three-component vector [number_enumerated, maximum_norm_found, matrix_of_vectors] with one of ±v per pair; flag=1 ignores m and returns [N,v] where v is a non-zero vector of length N ≤ b or [] if none; in flags 0/1 x must have integral entries and uses low-precision floating arithmetic for speed (error if large rounding errors); flag=2 robust (x can be non-integral real entries) but slower; if b omitted and m omitted potentially huge storage; examples include Leech lattice enumerations and advice about paresize memory parameter and alternative slower safe mode. Syntax: GEN qfminim0(GEN x, GEN b = NULL, GEN m = NULL, long flag, long prec). Alternatives: GEN minim (flag=0), GEN minim2 (flag=1), GEN minim_raw (do not perform LLL reduction and return NULL on accuracy error).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfnorm (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete function; use qfeval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfnorm(GEN x, GEN q = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qforbits (compute orbits under matrix group action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return orbits of set V under action of linear transformation group generated by G. Assumes G contains -identity and V contains only one of {v,-v}. If G does not stabilize V returns 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing representatives and lengths of orbits for automorphisms of lattice. Syntax: GEN qforbits(GEN G, GEN V).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfparam (parametrize solutions of ternary quadratic forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ternary quadratic form G and particular solution sol, return coefficients of binary quadratic forms that parametrize solutions; optional flag (0..3) chooses reduction of one of the forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default flag=0 (no reduction). Example demonstrates parametric representation. Syntax: GEN qfparam(GEN G, GEN sol, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfperfection (perfection rank of quadratic form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Output the perfection rank of positive definite quadratic form G: rank of family of symmetric matrices vivt where vi are minimal vectors (s half number of minimal vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires computing minimal vectors and can be lengthy. Syntax: GEN perf(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfrep (count representations by quadratic form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count vectors representing successive integers by positive definite integer quadratic form q up to bound B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag=0 count all vectors: output vector whose i-th entry is half the number of vectors v with q(v)=i (1 ≤ i ≤ B). Flag=1 count vectors of even norm: i-th entry is half the number with q(v)=2i. Uses naive algorithm based on qfminim and will fail if any entry grows beyond 2^31 (or 2^63) limits. Syntax: GEN qfrep0(GEN q, GEN B, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfsign (signature of quadratic form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return [p,m] where p is number of positive eigenvalues and m number of negative eigenvalues of symmetric matrix x; computed using Gaussian reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfsign(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfsolve (solve X^t G X = 0 over Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given square symmetric rational matrix G, solve X^t G X = 0 over Q; return a non-zero vector or matrix whose columns generate a totally isotropic subspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no solution returns an integer: a prime p such that no local solution at p, or -1 if no real solution, or -2 if n=2 and -det G positive but not a square. Examples illustrate return codes. Syntax: GEN qfsolve(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: seralgdep (algebraic dependency for power series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a linear relation between powers (1, s, ..., s^p) of series s with polynomial coefficients of degree ≤ r; return relation or 0 if none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series main variable must not be x to be able to express result as polynomial in x. Examples provided show usage. Syntax: GEN seralgdep(GEN s, long p, long r).

rubrics_metrics.name: setbinop (binary operation on sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return set of f(x,y) where x runs through X and y through Y; if Y omitted assume X=Y and f symmetric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: set addition, subtraction and doubling. Syntax: GEN setbinop(GEN f, GEN X, GEN Y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: setintersect (set intersection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection of two sets x and y; undefined if x or y not sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See setisset to check/set conversion. Syntax: GEN setintersect(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setisset (detect PARI set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return true (1) if x is a PARI ‘set’ (row vector with strictly increasing entries), false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convert any object into a set (useful for vectors) use Set. Examples show Set([3,1,1,2]) => [1,2,3]. Syntax: long setisset(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: setminus (set difference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return difference x \ y: elements of x not in y; undefined if x or y not sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN setminus(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: setsearch (search or insertion index in set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether x belongs to set S; default returns index j such that S[j]=x or 0 if not found. If flag non-zero return index where x should be inserted (0 if already present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S must be a set. If S is not a set, sorted lists with cmp order are allowed; otherwise undefined. Examples show listsort before searching and use with listinsert. Syntax: long setsearch(GEN S, GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: setunion (set union)
rubrics_metrics.description: Union of two sets x and y; undefined if x or y not sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN setunion(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: trace (generalized trace)
rubrics_metrics.description: For general x, trace equals sum of x and its conjugate (except for polmods where it's algebraic number trace). For square matrices it's the ordinary trace. For non-square (but not vector) matrices an error occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtrace(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecextract (extract components via mask/range/specifier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract components of vector or matrix x according to component specifier y (integer mask, vector of indices, or string describing range). Optional z for column specifier when x is matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integer y interpreted as binary mask (bits from right correspond to components from left). Vector y lists component numbers in specified order. String y can be single index, 'a..b' range (a or b may be omitted default 1..-1), negative indexes count from end, ^ prefix means complement. If z present x must be matrix; y is row specifier and z column specifier. Range notations v[i..j] and v[^i] are faster but lack reverse order and omitted endpoints. Examples provided. Syntax: GEN extract0(GEN x, GEN y, GEN z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsearch (search in sorted vector/list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether x belongs to sorted vector/list v; return positive index if found else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cmpf omitted assume v sorted by standard comparison lex (works for ints, fractions, reals and vectors thereof). If cmpf given assume v sorted according to it. By abuse matrix columns and transposed vectors are accepted. Unsorted input gives undefined result. Syntax: long vecsearch(GEN v, GEN x, GEN cmpf = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsort (stable mergesort with custom comparator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort vector x in ascending order using mergesort (stable). cmpf optional to control ordering (integer k, vector for lexicographic component order, or comparison function closure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cmpf options: integer k (sort by k-th subcomponent), vector (lexicographic order by listed components), closure (x,y)->int like sign function. Binary digits of flag: 1 => indirect sorting (return permutation), 4 => descending, 8 => remove duplicates w.r.t. comparator (keep first). Examples show custom comparators and advice to precompute expensive keys to avoid recomputation (e.g., combine vecsort and vecextract). Syntax: GEN vecsort0(GEN x, GEN cmpf = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecsum (sum vector components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return sum of components of vector v; return 0 for empty vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vecsum([1,2,3])=6, vecsum([])=0. Syntax: GEN vecsum(GEN v).

rubrics_metrics.name: vector (construct row vector by expression)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create row vector with n components given by expr evaluated at integer points 1..n for control variable X; omitted args fill zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variable X is lexically scoped per-element so changes inside expr do not affect subsequent iterations; examples show per-element local indexing and contrast with for-loop behavior. Syntax: vector(n,{X},{expr=0}).

rubrics_metrics.name: vectorsmall (construct small-integer vector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Like vector but returns t_VECSMALL (row vector of small integers) with n components computed from expr or zeros if omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when components are small integers for compact representation. Syntax parallels vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: vectorv (column vector construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: As vector, but returns a column vector (type t_COL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: vectorv(n,{X},{expr=0}).

rubrics_metrics.name: library loops and numerical routines introduction (section 3.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI provides preprogrammed loops (sums, products, recursions) and numerical routines (integration, summation of series) useful for GP programming; library mode routines require function pointer eval(E,x) to evaluate functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One parameter must be control variable (simple variable name). For library mode the function eval interface is described: GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN) with context eval(E,x). See Libpari manual for details.
